title: Block Talk - Episode #2 | Everything about the Binance hack, bitcoin price trend forecasts, and other current events

reels.title: How North Korean hackers got into Binance
reels.hook: The biggest crypto hack did not start through the front door
reels.why: A concrete story about a heist worth several billion with a clear sequence: a hacked engineer's laptop, massive payouts, and the Lazarus Group. The hook is right in the first sentence.
reels.speaker: Vedran Mijatović
reels.quote: Attacks on platforms, they never go through the front door.

cards.text: The biggest crypto hack did not start through the front door
Vedran Mijatović · Moj Kripto channel
Between 6.3 and 6.4 billion dollars was extracted from Binance.
Attacks on platforms never go through the front door.
cards.anchor: ne idu nikad na glavna vrata

cards.text: Entrance: the laptop of the engineer in charge of security
Lazarus Group, special hacker unit

reels.title: He stole billions. Why did the hacker have to flee to Thorchain?
reels.hook: He stole billions. Where to go with them in a couple of minutes?
reels.why: Tense escape logic step by step, including Uniswap, slippage, and freezing of funds. It ends with the clear point that only Thorchain was left for him.
reels.speaker: Vedran Mijatović
reels.quote: The only thing left for him is Thorchain.

cards.text: He stole billions. Where to go with them in a couple of minutes?
Vedran Mijatović · Moj Kripto channel
The hacker from Binance had to exit stablecoins before they freeze them.
That much you lose on slippage when you exchange 100 million dollars all at once
The only thing left for him is Thorchain.

reels.title: Why privacy coins are booming: KYC everywhere, and accountability nowhere
reels.hook: You give them all your data. And when they steal it?
reels.why: It evokes an emotion of injustice that the viewer recognizes from everyday life, and alongside that clearly explains two reasons for the hype around privacy coins.
reels.speaker: Vedran Mijatović
reels.quote: You have to give that by law, and when someone steals that from them, and they steal from them every day, well, then nothing to anyone.

cards.text: You give them all your data. And when they steal it?
Veljko Skenderija · host
Viewer's question: where did the hype around privacy coins come from in the past year?
Vedran Mijatović · Moj Kripto channel
And when someone steals that from them, and they steal from them every day, well, then nothing to anyone.
No company wants everyone to see who it sent money to

reels.title: Ban Thorchain? "That's like you ban Honda"
reels.hook: Hackers use it. Should it be banned?
reels.why: A short question from the host opens a clear stance on decentralization, and the analogy with Honda is a memorable point that closes the thought.
reels.speaker: Vedran Mijatović
reels.quote: The fact that someone abuses that, that is like I now go and ban Honda.

cards.text: Hackers use it. Should it be banned?
Vedran Mijatović · Moj Kripto channel
Thorchain did not block the swaps of the hacker who robbed Binance.
Protocol participants are everywhere across the world
That is like I now go and ban Honda.

reels.title: Monero or Zcash? Why opt-in privacy is a "scam"
reels.hook: A privacy coin that by default is not private?
reels.why: A sharp and concrete stance on Zcash, supported by a figure of under 30% of users. It ends with a strong argument about what hackers actually use.
reels.speaker: Vedran Mijatović
reels.quote: When a hacker wants to stash money, he will use either Monero or, I don't know, Thorchain and will not Zcash.

cards.text: A privacy coin that by default is not private?
Vedran Mijatović · Moj Kripto channel
A comparison of the two most famous privacy coins: Monero and Zcash.
That's that opt-in thing, and that means, to me that's a scam.
That many people use Zcash privately
When a hacker wants to stash money, he will use either Monero or Thorchain and will not Zcash.

reels.title: "Buy me Bitcoin for 100 euros": crypto is arriving in banks
reels.hook: Bitcoin soon in your mobile banking?
reels.why: A clear and practical insight into how banks are introducing crypto: from VIP clients to the average person. The picture of an ordinary client at the counter stays in the memory.
reels.speaker: Dean Rogulja
reels.quote: What interests him is that he sees it on his screen, in his mobile banking, and that is the whole story.

cards.text: Bitcoin soon in your mobile banking?
Dean Rogulja · Kripto Evolucija channel
After a series of hacks: where will average people keep crypto?
With us, Zaba recently started, via ETFs
"Here, buy me Bitcoin for 100 euros."
What interests him is that he sees it on his screen, in his mobile banking.

reels.title: Bitcoin at one million dollars? "I wouldn't be surprised"
reels.hook: Bitcoin for a million dollars: realistic or a fairy tale?
reels.why: A big round number attracts attention. The answer is rounded out and has an interesting twist: a million in ten years will not be worth the same as today.
reels.speaker: Vedran Mijatović
reels.quote: I wouldn't rule out that it will be a million dollars.

cards.text: Bitcoin for a million dollars: realistic or a fairy tale?
Veljko Skenderija · host
Willy Woo's model: 241–413 thousand $ by 2028, a million $ by 2033.
Vedran Mijatović · Moj Kripto channel
Scenario that Vedran does not rule out
In ten years, a million dollars is not the same as today.

reels.title: "Everyone loves Bitcoin." "Not everyone, Peter Schiff…"
reels.hook: Even JP Morgan now praises Bitcoin. Really everyone?
reels.why: A serious assertion that Bitcoin has become a normal asset is interrupted by a witty interjection about Peter Schiff. A short exchange with a humorous ending.
reels.speaker: Vedran Mijatović
reels.quote: I think Peter Schiff has a personal problem with Michael Saylor.
